scope: Light filesystem reads and scalar estimates only. No model, Torch import, GPU probe, service change, repository edit or running-job mutation.
finding: No clear accidental graph or startup-flag regression was found. Native HD full-sequence attention and CPU-cache/weight residency pressure are materially heavier than the old example. The sustained current slowdown is larger than attention scaling alone predicts; paging or driver residency pressure is plausible but not proven without a profiler.

current.estimateLimits: One observed later iteration, not a stable ETA; excludes decoding, finalization and any later residency changes.

unchangedGraphControlsVerified: SamplerCustom cfg=1, add_noise=true, seed=2026 and same conditioning/sampler links

staticWorkEstimates.method: Wan's 8x spatial VAE reduction, 2x2 spatial patching, 25 pose latent frames plus one reference frame, 5120 channels and 40 blocks from the installed native implementation.
staticWorkEstimates.limits: Estimates exclude quantization parameters, scales, temporary activations, Q/K/V projections, model/text/vision weights, transfer buffers, allocator overhead and WDDM/shared-memory behavior. They do not measure actual allocated or resident memory.

nativeExecutionEvidence: Engine log reports mixed-precision operations and native CUDA int8/convrot capabilities; Wan model weight/manual-cast dtype is FP16, not a new FP32 diffusion fallback.

Native WanAnimate2SelfAttention calls optimized_attention. The installed PyTorch attention path calls comfy.ops.scaled_dot_product_attention; its backend priority is FLASH_ATTENTION, CUDNN_ATTENTION, EFFICIENT_ATTENTION, then MATH.

The first sampling iteration runs the pose branch and fills its cache; later iterations reuse per-block cached inputs, dequantize/reproject K/V, and still run per-frame generation attention. At this geometry the generation branch has 26 frame calls per block across 40 blocks.

Startup --disable-smart-memory/--cache-none follows Aftertake's existing sequential policy; --disable-fast-disk/--async-offload 1 follows the explicit existing safe-weight-copy compatibility option. These flags do not disable optimized attention or send diffusion to CPU.

Triton was unavailable at engine startup, but native CUDA kernels and PyTorch SDPA remained available; nothing in this job newly removed Triton or selected an eager-only attention path. Actual per-call SDPA backend cannot be established from these logs.

pinnedMemoryClarification.meaning: A maximum registration allowance, not a preallocation. On Windows MAX_PINNED_MEMORY=0.40*physicalRAM.
pinnedMemoryClarification.actualAllocationAccounting: pin_memory registers an existing CPU tensor with cudaHostRegister and increments TOTAL_PINNED_MEMORY only after successful registration. The startup message does not reveal the live registered amount.

actionableConclusion: Preserve the running exact native graph and configuration; these reads do not justify restarting or changing its precision/kernels.
Avoid estimating this HD Wan job from the old five-minute example or the faster LTX/H3 runs. The observed second iteration alone is about 8.45 minutes.

If future capacity or throughput work is authorized, compare actual native attention backend and host/driver residency at a controlled completed-job boundary; do not infer that disabling cache, pinned memory or optimized paths will help.

Native static context windows could reduce full-sequence attention/cache pressure in a future explicit workflow variant, but would change the current graph and are not exposed or validated here. No such change was made.
